region: DataFeel Dot contact surface — activity-associated profile

loci.basis: NTC thermistor at contact surface. Mild warmth (36–40 °C) is associated with increased local metabolic activity and vasodilation. Thermoelectric element provides bidirectional control.

Normalised time-of-day (0.0 = midnight, 1.0 = midnight). Activity phase approximately 0.25–0.75 (06:00–18:00 local). Host-supplied; not measured by the device. Used as the ABR interior locus (B) to gate both haptic and optical outputs: when circadian phase is high (daytime), the gate is open and thermal disturbances drive stronger multimodal output.

170 Hz resonant actuator. Pacinian corpuscles are most sensitive in the 200–300 Hz range; 170 Hz is within the activation window. Vibrotactile stimulation at moderate amplitude activates large-diameter Aβ afferents, consistent with gate-control analgesic pathways. Activity profile uses higher amplitude and shorter pulse duration.

RGB blue channel, ~466 nm. Intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs) expressing melanopsin have peak sensitivity near 480 nm; 466 nm is within the activation range. Blue-enriched illumination during the active phase is associated with circadian synchronisation and suppression of melatonin secretion (Brainard et al., 2001; Thapan et al., 2001). This association is retinal and systemic, not a local tissue effect of the Dot LED.

relations.description: Thermal disturbance (A) drives haptic amplitude (R) gated by circadian phase (B). During the activity phase (B high), thermal changes produce stronger haptic response. During the rest phase (B low), haptic output is suppressed. Same gate as R-02 — both modalities are coupled through the same circadian interior locus, producing multimodal resonance in the activity window.

Thermal disturbance (A) drives blue optical output (R) gated by circadian phase (B). During the activity phase (B high), thermal changes produce blue-enriched illumination consistent with daytime circadian entrainment. The same circadian gate as R-01 means haptic and optical outputs are simultaneously expressed in the same circadian window — this is the area of multimodal intersection.
